references.text: The same measure of wine for a drink offering (a quarter hin) is mentioned in connection with the daily offering, showing the standard measure for drink offerings in Israelite sacrificial practice.
A drink offering of wine is mentioned as part of the grain offering, and the expression 'an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord' is used in the same way.
It specifies the amount of wine for the drink offering: half a hin for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb, expanding on the regulations from chapter 15.
Earlier in the same chapter, a quarter hin of wine is mentioned as the drink offering for each lamb, as part of the gradual increase in offering amounts based on the size of the animal.
A third of a hin of wine for a ram is mentioned, showing the structure where half a hin for a bull is the largest measure ratio in this sacrificial law.
The expression 'an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord' (אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ־נִיחֹחַ לַיהוָה) is used at the consecration of priests, using the same wording as in Num 15:10.
Jacob poured out a drink offering (נֶסֶךְ) at Bethel, showing the early use of drink offerings in the patriarchal period before the formal legislation.
